note: The first Unit where the full NFR set binds: U1 was a library and U2 a spec Unit, so most inception NFRs were N/A with a structural reason. Here a process, a database, a network boundary and a screen arrive at once. Two requirements changed under scrutiny and both are recorded as corrections: the OTP hash reversed from a password hash to HMAC when measured (bcrypt buys hours at 58ms per issue; HMAC under a server-held key defeats the offline attack outright at ~1us), and the ceiling check order was corrected at review from global-first to narrowest-first, since global-first lets one attacker spend every teacher's allowance before their own limit trips. No latency target and no availability SLO are stated, deliberately - nothing has been measured and one instance has no failover, so an invented number would be weakened on first contact rather than investigated.

coverage.target: Android target and compile SDK - owned by U10 release-packaging. This Unit ships Compose screens but not the build configuration
Device floor and AAB size - owned by U10
observability NFR8.7 and functional-spec §3 - both language bundles ship on screen one, so a Bangla layout break is found here rather than on screen forty. OTP entry is one of the five named screens
Offline reads - Room is a read cache owned by the feature Units; U3 has no cached domain list
Offline writes - permitted for the mid-class path only, which is U5's

performance NFR6.1-NFR6.3, NFR6.7 and scalability NFR10.1-NFR10.2 - 100 teachers is not a throughput problem; the binding constraint is the worker count, which makes the datastore-backed counter a correctness requirement
security NFR7.1-NFR7.4 - the SMS ceiling with sub-ceilings beneath it, every outcome consuming budget, and an alert verified in staging. This is where an attacker spends the project's money directly
Data residency - no requirement; nearest region is an Infrastructure Design concern
Money representation - no money crosses this Unit's surface. U1 owns the type and U2 the schema assertion
Children's data encrypted at rest - a hosting-tier property owned by Infrastructure Design. This Unit's schema is what will be encrypted
security T3 and functional-spec §3 - no device identifier is transmitted, and the phone number is typed rather than read from the SIM

The seven abuse controls as BR2.1-BR2.7, plus security T6 and T7. The ceiling order was corrected at review from global-first to narrowest-first, and the existence-oracle defence extended from hash symmetry to write symmetry
security NFR13.1-NFR13.2 and reliability NFR13.3 - family invalidation on reuse, enforced 15-minute expiry, no role or lens claim in the token, and a gateway timeout recorded as UNKNOWN
security NFR14.1-NFR14.3 - the table split, row-level security, and the non-superuser meta-test without which the other two certify nothing
Accessibility and back-stack behaviour - the Android surface here is OTP entry and the lens switcher; the back-stack privacy case AC9.4.2 arrives with the guardian child switch at B5
Inherited from U2: this Unit adds three routes to the committed contract, and the schema-diff gate catches any drift
Backend coverage floor applies. The authorization layer is measured as BRANCH coverage rather than line, because lens resolution is pure branching and line coverage on it is close to meaningless
